steps.speaker: FAC Officer
steps.content: It's no use—the shell's too tough! We can't break through!

The FAC forces' persistent long-range assaults have reached a deadlock with the expanding Mania wisteria. Although the contamination's expansion has slowed, human efforts prove incapable of eradicating it entirely.
Back and forth the vines sway in an endless cycle, akin to a frenzied creature desperately clutching at survival. The situation has regressed into yet another impasse.

steps.speaker: FAC Officer
steps.content: Is it because it's rooted in the Rust? The monster's growing even faster now—don't tell me it's feeding on the nearby Corruptors too?

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: It could also be that DisCity's standard equipment isn't fully compatible with Eastian Mania. Not to mention this contamination has been festering for over a century.

As it continues to stretch skyward, its shadow engulfs more and more of the city districts. Under this looming unknown threat, civilians are forced to evacuate in growing numbers—and those who have been fighting it for so long are beginning to lose their patience.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: HQ is rushing to recalibrate our equipment based on Eastia's intel. It should be fully operational in about four hours. In the meantime, all we need to do is hold the line. We must ensure complete containment and prevent any contamination from seeping out.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: Once the weapons are in place, we can inflict maximum damage on the Mania entity. Now that it has no hostages, we won't need to hold back anymore.
But before then, we still have four hours to wait.
There's still time for another operation plan, isn't it?

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: An unknown threat from Eastia is no trivial matter, even for DisCity. With Paradeisos seeking to establish relations with Eastia, any friction between the two sides at this point would be diplomatically disastrous.
Give me more time. I'll get to the bottom of this.

steps.speaker: FAC Officer
steps.content: But that's far too dangerous! What if something happens to you?

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: I'll find another way—a safe way. Trust me...
You also want to trust that person... This can't be left unresolved.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: ...Chief, you only have four hours.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: Please, make sure you come back safely.

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: I understand. Thank you, everyone.
With only four hours remaining, you can neither approach the wisteria nor use the shackles to re-enter the illusion.
But you still have one last option—
[Scene transition: Taleteller's cell]

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: Let's talk, Yugu. I know you've returned from the fete.

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: That fete wasn't yours to begin with. Its true host drove out all the "visitors"—including you, who were seeking refuge there.
The Eastian woman, who had been lounging in repose, finally shows a smile as she slowly opens her eyes.

steps.speaker: Yugu
steps.content: I suppose you have already uncovered the truth about the fete, rescued the hostages, and broken free from the illusion. With such feats accomplished, you should be ready to take decisive action... Why come looking for me, of all things?

steps.speaker: Yugu
steps.content: Do not tell me you have come for a story now...

steps.speaker: Yugu
steps.content: Tired of Yingying's happy endings? Have you at last thought of seeking me out for something more... thrilling?

steps.speaker: %u
steps.content: I don't want stories. I want the truth.
She rises—hair loose and feet bare—and draws uncomfortably close. A cold, unsettling breeze brushes against your cheek as she fixes her gaze on your eyes.

steps.speaker: Yugu
steps.content: The truth... Whether it is facts or truth you are after, has the Eastian scholar not given you that already? All encapsulated in such neat words.

steps.speaker: Yugu
steps.content: Cruel, heartless, insignificant—and eventually, forgotten by all. With your experience, I believe you can envision such a fate? I doubt it would bring you joy. After all, such narratives are seldom favored... Oh, except for me.

steps.speaker: Yugu
steps.content: I pity them, hold a fondness for them. I spice up those tales with passion and romance, only to draw in a few sensation-seeking listeners. But at least in doing so, they would be known by others—and those poor souls wouldn't die entirely in vain. Though I suppose my approach is not quite to your taste.
Even through her veil, you can see her smile growing increasingly unhinged.

steps.speaker: Yugu
steps.content: It seems that you, like many others, favor stories where goodness prevails and all ends well, unable to stomach the cruel indifference of fate and its bitter partings. Perhaps you'd like me to embellish things? To paint you a blissful ending like that adorable flower spirit did, just to offer solace to your conscience?

steps.speaker: Yugu
steps.content: Heh, I suppose I could do that. Just like I indulge those sensation-seeking patrons of mine, I can satisfy your desires as well.
You feel a compelling urge to refute her.

You know that whether it's her tales supposedly born out of compassion or the audience she claims to humbly serve—the taleteller holds no regard for either. To her, everyone, both within and beyond her narratives, is merely prey for her twisted entertainment.
Now she lifts her veil, ready to speak, her gaze gleaming with delight as she prepares to tear you apart—like a butcher towering over their next sacrifice.
But in the end, you decide to change the subject.
...There's no need. I'm not here to hear stories. I only want to know... about the people there. About what really happened to those who lived and breathed through it all.
I need your power.
Yingying may be the host of the fete, but it was you who brought her to DisCity. Before the Mania outbreak, you were the one sending us all into the fete.
You captured both Yingying and the fete within your book, didn't you? That's how you can make people experience it all again, reopening the path to the fete.

steps.speaker: Yugu
steps.content: All right, I will stop making fun of you. I know you want to return to that street, to see that person again. Very well, I will help you.

steps.speaker: Yugu
steps.content: This is precisely the story I was hoping for.

steps.speaker: Yugu
steps.content: However, out of concern for your well-being, allow me to offer one word of caution.

steps.speaker: Yugu
steps.content: Remember, don't chase after impossible desires. Don't make the same mistake... that she did.
But the look in her eyes tells a different story—she evidently anticipates that you'll make the same exact mistake. You've seen through her game since long ago.
The taleteller removes her veil, her rosy lips parting softly. The pages of the book flutter in her hands, characters floating free, coiling around you and drawing you into their depths.
